messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a small spike of 413s on /v1/embeddings when clients send mixed-dim batches around 380–420KB. Notably the errors correlate with our router shard that enforces 4MB shard limit + per-request byte ceiling.

rana: Do you have examples? Is it always the same client or mixed dims?

maria: Mixed dims. Samples attached to the incident ticket (link). Pattern: client sends 100 short vectors + 3 long ones, server tries to coalesce by bytes and ends up with a single oversized route. We currently split only by count, not by bytes+dim.

tim: Noted. Our splitter heuristics are count-first because that was simpler, but it breaks when token dims vary a lot. We should switch to a 'byte-aware' splitter: prefer splitting so that route_byte_estimate <= ROUTE_SIZE_THRESHOLD (e.g., 256KB) and also ensure per-vector dims compatibility.

oliver: Agree. Also UX ask: console should surface when auto-splitting happened and why (size vs dims vs quota). Right now it just shows a slow request and a 413 in routing logs — ops can't tell if it was client payload or router decision.

maria: Proposal: new router fields in telemetry: `split_reason` = ["bytes","dim_mismatch","count"], `split_plan` = "N->M" (e.g., "103->2"), and `split_origin` = ["client","router_auto"]. Expose as per-request tags in the console request view.

rana: +1 on those tags. Implementation detail: we should emit a single event `embed.split_attempt` with properties {estimated_bytes, actual_bytes, reason, plan, routes_returned}. We already have `embed.prefetch` events — keep naming consistent.

tim: For an initial rollout, router should fallback gracefully: if split fails (race with quota/shard), return a structured 413 with `retry_after` and `split_hint` so clients can retry smarter. Example payload: 
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
{
  "error": "request_too_large",
  "split_hint": {"max_route_bytes": 262144, "recommended_chunks": 3},
  "retry_after": 1.5
}
```

oliver: For quotas: do we count units pre- or post-split? If we count pre-split then a malicious large request could blow quota calculations. We should count by final routed units, and also emit `quota.estimate_pre_split` and `quota.final_charged_units`. Ops needs both for auditing.

maria: Yes, charge final routed units. Also console UX: show both estimated and actual charged units in the request detail panel. Add an annotation when the request crossed a per-route soft-threshold (e.g., 200KB) so PMs can see which clients push big requests.

rana: Two engineering notes: 1) bumping split heuristics means more prefix/KV cache misses — we should add a metric `kv_cache_evictions_from_splits` to watch perf impact. 2) Add a feature flag `embed.byte_aware_splitter_v1` to rollout to 10% of traffic.

tim: Recommend rollout plan: A/B 10% -> 33% -> 100% over 2 weeks, with automatic rollback if tail latencies worsen by >20ms or kv cache miss rate increases by >2pp. Dashboard: new panel 'embed/splitter' showing split_rate, average_routes_per_request, split_reason_breakdown, kv_cache_eviction_rate.

maria: I'll draft the console wire for the request detail: add a small pill after latency that says `split: auto(bytes)` or `split: client` and a tooltip with the split_plan + charged units.

oliver: Also add an alert on unexpected rise of `split_reason=bytes` (threshold >5% of embed traffic over 5m) — that often indicates client regressions or a model size change.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature flag `embed.byte_aware_splitter_v1` created (rollout: 10%) by rana. CI pipeline: embed-splitter tests passed (45/45).

maria: Great. Action items: rana implement telemetry events + feature flag, tim update router split logic + graceful 413 body, oliver add dashboard & alerts, I'll make console wire and update docs. I'll post a short RFC with code sketch.

rana: I'll open PR and link tests. Quick pseudo for splitter logic to include in RFC: 
```
def byte_aware_split(items, max_route_bytes=262144):
    routes = []
    cur = []
    cur_bytes = 0
    for it in items:
        est = estimate_vector_bytes(it)
        if cur and cur_bytes + est > max_route_bytes:
            routes.append(cur)
            cur = [it]
            cur_bytes = est
        else:
            cur.append(it)
            cur_bytes += est
    if cur: routes.append(cur)
    return routes
```

tim: Looks good. Also make sure `estimate_vector_bytes` accounts for JSON framing and compression heuristics we use in the router.

maria: Thanks all — will track RFC and link the incident ticket. :)
